subject: linearComb() and backTransform(): Interpretation and Values if formula includes quadratic terms

messages.author: 2d3b494e6d0830e8
messages.subject: linearComb() and backTransform(): Interpretation and Values if formula includes quadratic terms
parts:
Hi Everyone!

Sorry if these are really basic questions (and probably not solely related to unmarked), but I have  been stuck with linearComb() and could not find the answers to my questions in the FAQ, the vignette or here (although I am very sorry if it is already covered somewhere). 
I am using pcount() for the estimation of abundance and detection of single season data of different species (one model per species) with M = 55 sites and J = 8 visits (all sites had 8 visits). My obsCovs (time after sunrise, day of year, number of other individuals present) were scaled using the scale() function, my SiteCovs (proportional area of open, forest and urban area at each site) are not scaled but just devided by 100 (eg. 40,20,20 for 40% open, 20% forest and urban habitat). Except for cases where a site only consists of 1 habitat, they never sum up to 100% because of other habitats  and to avoid collinearity. 
My problem is the interpretation and transformation of estimates when my best model includes quadratic terms in the state and/or det process. 

Those are the estimates I get for one of my species:
StateEstimates:
     (Intercept)      Forest_Area I(Forest_Area^2) 
       -1.401179         8.266376        -5.356210

DetEstimates
   (Intercept)      StartTime I(StartTime^2) 
    -1.2629669     -1.0653560     -0.8903796

My Questions are:
1.) due to the horrendous estimates, I assume backTransform() is not applicable to my type = "state" estimates (makes sence), but how can I backtransform them manually, ?
2.) what will backTransform(linearComb(BestModel, coefficients =  DetEstimates)) exactly output, what do the estimated numbers say? Mean det / abundance per site? 
3.) let's suppose, I want to plot the influence of StartTime on the Detection: I know I have to create a matrix specifying values for each of the coefficients and calculate each linearComb(), but what do i put in for these?
As I specified StartTime in minutes after sunrise, will I just use "60" for the estimate 1 hour after sunrise, or do I have to use the a transformed version of this number? What can I use for the squared Starttime? simply the sqrt(StartTime) (or the transformed version)?

With writing, I realised how basic these questions must have to be for some of you. however, for me they are not, so I hope you don't mind me asking them here. 
Thx for your time and, hopefully, answers to my questions, Christian
